 Print Refused to surrender, opened fire: LeT commander Lateef Bhat killed in Kulgam NEW DELHI: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander and most wanted terrorist Lateef Bhat was killed by security forces on Wednesday, hours after an encounter broke out in Jammu and Kashmir 's Kulgam district, news agency PTI reported. Bhat was trapped inside a mosque in the cordoned-off area and had refused repeated appeals to surrender, instead opening fire on security forces. The encounter began early Wednesday morning, shortly before mosques across the Valley announced morning prayers. "Congratulations guys. Some dishes are best served cold, even in cold weather," DG CRPF GP Singh said. Security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area of south Kashmir following specific intelligence inputs. Officials said Bhat was trapped inside the cordon and was repeatedly urged to lay down his arms. Earlier, SSP Kulgam said security forces were exercising "maximum restraint" as Bhat was firing from inside a mosque. He had said forces would take the time necessary to neutralise him while ensuring minimal damage to the religious structure. The encounter comes two days after security forces killed Umar Nisar Dar, another suspected terrorist linked to the November 11 attack on a CRPF post in Kulgam, in a gunfight near Laru bypass on Monday. Bhat, however, managed to escape from the encounter site. Both Bhat and Dar were suspected of carrying out the attack, which left three paramilitary personnel injured. Following Dar's killing, security forces continued search operations in the area to track down Bhat. They re-established contact with him during searches early Wednesday, triggering a fresh exchange of fire. Join conversation

 Officials said Dar had allegedly sheltered Bhat and provided him with logistical support for nearly six months. The duo was also suspected of conducting reconnaissance before targeting the CRPF post. Kashmir Zone Police had announced the encounter on X, saying, "Encounter started with terrorists and joint party of JKP and SF in Kulgam." Dar, a former breadmaker who had been reported missing by his family, was killed a week after joining The Resistance Front (TRF), an offshoot of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba.
